head: ca8e077

rungs.name: two-servers
rungs.lesson: one file, run twice, is one replicated object; Ctrl-C one and the other carries on

rungs.name: server-client
rungs.lesson: a seed makes a server; a bare `fero(name)` finds it by name, follows it, and writes back

rungs.name: one-write
rungs.lesson: a client's write is a request: a `pending` row until a server stamps it; only then does it show, on both screens

rungs.name: rows
rungs.lesson: a write is a record (type, key, value) you can watch land; a row is written whole or by its fields, never both; a refused write never lands

rungs.name: views
rungs.lesson: an operator on `f.data` is a live view: it prints itself once, then only when a write moves a row across its edge or rewrites one it holds

rungs.name: numbers
rungs.lesson: a sale is a new row, never edited; `sum`, `avg`, `median`… are live numbers folded from the rows — tap one, never read-modify-write a total

rungs.name: ordered
rungs.lesson: a sorted view is an array in rank order: by a column, by a comparator with a tiebreak, the top n; a bounded window rotates in one batch

rungs.name: methods
rungs.lesson: a function under `methods:` runs on the server: a client awaits it, the reply follows the commit, and declaring them is the door

rungs.name: live
rungs.lesson: a method that returns a view streams: `await` it for a snapshot, `.open()` it for a live mirror the operators chain on; `close()` ends it

rungs.name: confirm
rungs.lesson: the same write awaited at three rungs — committed, replicated, persisted; the reply names the rung it PROVED, and a reject is how far it got, never a rollback

rungs.name: validation
rungs.lesson: `seams.validation` is one rule for every write that enters a server — the seed, its own, a client's; a refused write never shows, only a `rejected` row of `cluster.writes` with the reason

rungs.name: durable
rungs.lesson: `dir` makes the node durable: run the file again and it is the SAME node in its next life (`~2`), its rows back before it has a socket; the seed applies once; a solo `persisted` is one disk

rungs.name: cluster-of-three
rungs.lesson: three members on fixed addresses with disks: kill one, the two left vote it out in about a second and still prove `persisted` on two disks, and the same command brings the dead one back as itself from its disk

rungs.name: failover
rungs.lesson: `kill -9` the server feeding a client: its `peers` drops at once, its live handle re-subscribes by itself, its next write commits on a survivor (after the vote if the dead one stamped that row), and a call in flight fails fast unless `{ retry: true }`

rungs.name: static-topology
rungs.lesson: with the directory off every address is in the call — a member is `listen` + `hosts`, a client is `hosts` — and a shape that cannot work is refused at `fero()`

rungs.name: scoped
rungs.lesson: `replicas: 2` puts every row on exactly two members: a shard is never shown as the resource — a sync read or an operator throws typed, `await f.data` gathers the whole, a row not held is one hop away, and a client reads the union

rungs.name: lww-honesty
rungs.lesson: two members read a cell and write it back plus one, and one increment is lost — a cell keeps its last writer; write one row per event and fold them instead

rungs.name: inside
rungs.lesson: every instance carries a diagnostics handle off the typed surface: the journal, the log, compaction on demand, and a capture file the debugger opens

rungs.name: journal
rungs.lesson: `diag(f).journal(from)` is a cursor over the kernel's one diagnostics ring: tail it and watch a peer arrive and be voted in, leave by vote, and its link close

rungs.name: time-travel
rungs.lesson: a capture with a story: two writes before the first view are an election (`lww-lost` in the viewer), the same two after it are plain history, a cut heals by anti-entropy, and the scrubber replays any step

rungs.name: live
rungs.lesson: a running cluster writes a `kind: 'live'` capture file once a second (temp file, then rename) and `npm run debug -- <file>` polls it: the debugger follows a real fero process on this box with no wire attach

rungs.name: fleet-audit
rungs.lesson: real processes, real disks, real `kill -9`: three durable members, sensors writing facts through the door with receipts, a live dashboard, one member killed and then all three, restored from disk — then an audit: the members agree, every `persisted` receipt is on every member, no phantom rows, and a reject is not a rollback

rungs.name: chat
rungs.lesson: a chat is facts plus one sorted view: `post` runs on the server, throws its rule for every joiner and stamps who (`ctx.peer`) and when; every screen sorts the rows itself with a tiebreak, so they all agree
rungs.terminals: `node room.ts general` · `node join.ts general ada` · `node join.ts general bob`

rungs.name: kanban
rungs.lesson: a card is a row written by its fields: two editors change two fields of one card at once and both land; one rule, carried by the board and every editor, refuses a whole row or an unknown column — an editor refuses its own before it leaves

rungs.name: web-bridge
rungs.lesson: fero speaks TCP, so a browser reaches a resource through a Node bridge that is a bare client: `connect` records streamed to each tab as events, a form post written as a whole row

rungs.name: ledger
rungs.lesson: money is facts: transfers are rows on three durable members, the rule thrown from a method, the intent cleared through the door, every id on a member that comes back

rungs.name: sell
rungs.lesson: an open server lets every client change every row, the price included; declaring `methods:` is the door: the same write is refused `methods-only`, and `sell` writes the sale at the server's price

tiers: Four tiers: 01-17 climb one feature at a time, 20-23 open the debugger, 30 is everything at once on one box, and 40-44 are apps, the last of them the story the website tells: an open shop anyone can change, then the same shop behind a door.
runs: No build, no flags — Node 22.18+ or 23.6+ runs the `.ts` files as they are, after one `npm install` at the repo root (fero's one dependency).

vote.text: The link drops at once; the vote waits for the dead member's redials to give up — five tries, about a second at 30 ms, about four at the default 100.
